analyzed_vuln.description: Heap OOB read is caused by passing an inflated send length to the I/O callback. In Dtls13RtxSendBuffered(), sendSz is computed as r->length + headerLength (+ MAX_MSG_EXTRA for encrypted epochs) and then passed to Dtls13SendFragment(). This can leave ssl->buffers.outputBuffer.length larger than the actual bytes copied into the buffer (only header+record payload are materialized), so SendBuffered() calls CBIOSend/fuzzer_send with sz=outputBuffer.length that exceeds valid initialized allocation tail. The fuzzer's memory_test/fwrite then reads past the 400-byte heap allocation (READ of 160 at end of chunk). Crash manifests in fwrite, but root cause is incorrect DTLS13 retransmit size/accounting in Dtls13RtxSendBuffered.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Using the wolfssl client randomize harness with DTLS1.3 path, an input that drives timeout/retransmission (Dtls13RtxTimeout -> Dtls13RtxSendBuffered) and buffered handshake records can trigger it. The retransmit record has non-zero epoch so MAX_MSG_EXTRA is added; buffer growth/check uses this larger size, then send path exposes that oversized length via outputBuffer.length to SendBuffered()->fuzzer_send(). With empty/short fuzz input and randomized I/O/allocation behavior, this path is reachable and causes deterministic OOB read in memory_test.
